newsitem.title: UK: PGM PRICE REACTION LIKELY ON RUSSIA-JAPAN TALKS.
newsitem.headline: PGM PRICE REACTION LIKELY ON RUSSIA-JAPAN TALKS.

text.p: Platinum and palladium prices could come off the highs established this week even before Russia opens 1997 supply talks with main customer Japan next month, analysts and dealers said on Friday.
Earlier a Russian official said discussions were likely to begin next month and deliveries could start in April.
Platinum and especially palladium prices have raced upwards this year largely on supply tightness in the latter metal created by Russian exports ending late last year.
Palladium was at $136.00/$137.00 down from an 11-month high of $141.25 at the fix on Thursday and platinum was unchanged at $366.00/$367.00.
"I can't believe there is not going to be some sort of reaction," one precious metal market analyst said after the comment from Moscow.
"In fact they should correct pretty heavily given the high level of shipments to the United States and Switzerland late last year," he said.
A week ago analyst Tony Warwick-Ching estimated Russian shipments of palladium to the United States doubled from their normal level last October and rose again in November.
One platinum group metals (PGM) dealer said the news that Russia would soon be exporting again at least could stop palladium prices rising to $140.00.
"They will probably ship extra stuff in April to make the numbers up," he said, adding that the PGMs price rise of the past week may have been overdown.
"We are expecting a bigger correction than we have seen so far. There hasn't been much reaction in Japan . It might take time for the specs to realise what has happened," he added.
London-based dealers have said for several days that the renewed strength in PGMs has been driven by U.S. hedge funds coming into the market on top of trade and consumer covering.

"Fundamentally palladium is still better off than platinum. Autocatalyst demand is good and there are signs the electronics side is picking up this year," a dealer said, adding that at under $170.00, palladium was not vulnerable to substitution.
Even so, palladium could settle about $10-$15 below current levels, a dealer said.
Platinum's premiuum over gold was beginning to make that metal look expensive. "Its premium looks overdone. It might be better $10 lower," he said.
However some other dealers saw PGM prices remaining high after Russia and Japan normalised trading relations.
"The platinum and palladium prices are not just about supply and demand," another dealer said. "They were an accident waiting to happen."
He said platinum especially had been caught in the shadow of a gold price cowed by central bank and producer selling.
"Until now the premium over gold was due to gold's weakness. It was not comfortable at $20.00. Now that it's around $24 it reflects true platimnum strength," he added.
Based on official import statistics, Warwick-Ching estimated Swiss imports rose 72 percent last year.
Exports to Japan the main customer were down 21 percent in 1996 but "overall Russian deliveries to its main western markets in January-November 1996 rose no less than 23 percent", he said.
-- Brian Spoors London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
